title: Quasi-finiteness descends for a finitely presented affine model
statement: Let $(I,\leq)$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, let $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ be a directed system of commutative rings, and let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ be its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a finitely presented $A_{i_0}$-algebra $B_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $B_i=A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$ for $i\geq i_0$ and $B=A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$; these tensor products of commutative algebras are the pushouts whose spectra are the affine fibre products [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. If $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], then for some $i\geq i_0$ the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is quasi-finite.

source.place: Tag 094M, label lemma-descend-quasi-finite, specialized to affine schemes; Situation label situation-descent-property (Tag 081D).

proof.text: Restrict to J = {i : i₀ ≤ i}. The inclusion is final: every index has a common upper bound with i₀, and parallel arrows in a poset coincide. Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv therefore gives the same base colimit. Define B_j as the pushout of A_i₀ → A_j and b₀, with transition maps induced by the pushout universal property. Its cocone has point pushout(c.ι_i₀,b₀). To prove this cocone is colimiting, descend the left legs of a compatible cocone by the base colimit, and take its right leg at the initial tail index. The cocone identities show that every right leg equals this one. The pushout universal property gives the unique induced map. This is the explicit IsColimit construction in the Lean proof.

Finite presentation of b₀ implies finite type. RingHom.finiteType_isStableUnderBaseChange.pushout_inl gives finite type of every left pushout inclusion. For i ≤ j, cancel the initial pushout square from the later one by IsPushout.of_top. This identifies the canonical comparison from the successive pushout with the inverse of the unique pushout comparison isomorphism. ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso gives its surjectivity.

The quasi-finite hypothesis gives open singletons in the scheme fibres. Transport each such singleton by fiberHomeo; discreteTopology_iff_isOpen_singleton gives discreteness of each set-theoretic fibre. Mathlib locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isDiscrete_preimage_singleton applies, using the given local finite-type conjunct. After base change to the spectrum of any residue field, IsLocallyArtinian.of_locallyQuasiFinite makes the source locally Artinian, so discrete. Then topologicalKrullDim_zero_of_discreteTopology bounds its dimension by zero. The isomorphisms from the chosen ring colimits to the explicit cocone points commute with the induced ring map, as checked by colimit.hom_ext. Thus the same bound applies to colimMap φ. Apply exists_stage_fibre_dimension_le with d = 0, the finite-type maps and the surjective comparisons.

At the resulting stage, the finite-type map of spectra is locally of finite type. For p in Spec A_i, Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso and pullback.map identify the pullback using the algebraic residue field with its scheme-theoretic fibre; transport dimension by the induced homeomorphism. The fibre projection to Spec κ(p) is locally of finite type, so LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian makes the fibre locally Noetherian. Mathlib IsLocallyArtinian.of_topologicalKrullDim_le_zero then makes it locally Artinian, and hence discrete. Every singleton of the form asFiber x is open. The affine map is quasi-compact. Assemble these three conjuncts of Scheme.Hom.IsQuasiFinite and return the index with its defining inequality i₀ ≤ i. This argument also applies to empty fibres and the zero ring.
